name: Familialism
summary: Familialism gives priority to the family, usually the nuclear family of father, mother and children, as the basic unit and foundation of society, placing family needs above individual ones. In politics it appears as family-values conservatism, pro-natalist and pro-marriage policy, opposition to divorce, abortion and alternative family forms, and welfare systems that rely on families rather than the state for care.
scope: The mainstream Western and Catholic-Christian strand as documented on Wikipedia: Louis de Bonald's traditionalism, the Catholic teaching of John Paul II's Familiaris Consortio, and modern family-values movements and parties (Family First, Focus on the Family, Singapore's PAP). It also covers familialist welfare regimes of Southern Europe. It excludes the term's use in psychology and sociology as a neutral measure of family orientation, and the critics' use of it in Deleuze and Guattari. Most economic, foreign-policy and institutional statements are not addressed by the sources, so they are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Louis de Bonald
keyFigures.role: French traditionalist who modelled political society on the family and fought to repeal divorce

keyFigures.name: Pope John Paul II
keyFigures.role: Author of Familiaris Consortio, the leading modern Catholic statement on family rights and duties

sources.title: Familialism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, nuclear family as foundation, family-state analogy, familialist welfare, family-values politics, parties and critics.

sources.author: Pope John Paul II
sources.usedFor: Indissolubility of marriage, abortion, state limits on births, parents' educational rights, subsidiarity, mothers' work, family rights.

sources.title: Louis de Bonald
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Bonald's family-state analogy, divorce repeal, primogeniture, guilds, opposition to democracy and separation of powers.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Familialism is not an economic doctrine; Bonald attacked laissez-faire while US family-values conservatives usually back markets, so adherents split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Familialism has no stated tax doctrine; family tax allowances matter more to it than rates on the rich. Adherents split by wing.

unions-good.rationale: Bonald sought to restore guilds and corporate bodies, but modern family-values conservatives are often wary of unions; no settled position.

property-fundamental.rationale: Bonald defended inherited family estates and primogeniture, implying a strong property tie to the family line; modern sources say little.

cut-welfare.rationale: Familialist welfare logic expects families to provide care, but pro-family parties also back family benefits, so the wings pull in opposite directions.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No familialist source addresses surveillance; the ideology is indifferent on it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not a familialist question; adherents split between free-speech and order concerns.

strong-leader.rationale: Bonald favored strong centralized authority, but modern familialism is not tied to a strongman; split.

state-harmful.rationale: Familialism values social order and gives the state a protective role toward the family; the Wikipedia article even models the state on the family. Anarchism is alien to it.

decide-locally.rationale: Familiaris Consortio invokes subsidiarity, with the family first and the state helping, which favors lower levels; no explicit statement on regions.

traditional-family.rationale: The Wikipedia article defines familialism by the claim that the nuclear family is the basic unit and foundation of society and civilization.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Familialist parties such as Australia's Family First Party and the Singaporean government oppose same-sex parenting and adoption, and the article says alternative family forms are generally opposed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Familiaris Consortio counts the scourge of abortion among the threats to the family (para 6) and condemns state-imposed abortion programs (para 30).

more-religion-public.rationale: The family is tied to Christian teaching in the main strands; Familiaris Consortio asks the state to help parents give a faith-conforming education, but secular familialism exists.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Wikipedia article treats the family as the model for community and nation, and pro-family parties couple family with national tradition.

gradual-change.rationale: Bonald's traditionalism defended inherited institutions against revolutionary change; modern familialism is likewise defensive of existing family forms.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Pronatalist familialists often prefer births to immigration, but familialism as such does not define a migration policy; adherents vary.

revolution-justified.rationale: Bonald opposed the Revolution and held that disorder follows from broken order; familialism values stability.

experts-over-public.rationale: Familiaris Consortio calls parents' educational right original and irreplaceable against outside authorities; no direct statement on experts generally.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Bonald fought partitive inheritance and defended primogeniture to keep family estates intact, so heavy inheritance taxes cut against the family line.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Bonald sought to restore guilds and corporate bodies after the Le Chapelier Law, but modern familialism does not carry this.

one-party-rule.rationale: Not a familialist position; family-first parties compete in elections (Family First, League of Polish Families).

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a monarch who rules, and the statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state, on which the sources cited here are silent.

reviewHistory.rationale: Bonald held the monarch embodies the general will, modelling the state on the family; the Wikipedia article says the family-state analogy justified monarchy. Modern adherents are mostly indifferent.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a monarch who rules, and the statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state, on which the sources cited here are silent.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

democracy-best.rationale: Bonald rejected shared sovereignty, while modern family-values parties work within democracy, so the strands divide.

natural-rulers.rationale: The family-state analogy casts rulers as fathers and subjects as children, which grounds natural authority; the Wikipedia article cites Aristotle on household rule.

separate-church-state.rationale: Familiaris Consortio ties family and Church closely and asks public authority to support religious upbringing; Christian-right familialists oppose strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Bonald and Kuehnelt-Leddihn tie the family to Christian teaching, but modern familialists generally want family law to reflect it, not direct scripture rule.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Familialism does not define the nation ethnically; some strands do, most do not.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Familialism sees the family as basis of society; Engels and Marx appear in the article as its critics because they tied the family to class society.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Familialism puts family needs above individual needs, which rejects individual self-interest as the moral basis.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Familiaris Consortio frames the family's rights through duties and mission to society; the Wikipedia article says family needs come before the individual's.

limit-population.rationale: Familiaris Consortio (para 30) condemns public authority limiting couples' decisions about children and imposed birth programs.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Bonald criticized the Industrial Revolution for weakening family life, but modern familialism does not call it a disaster.

restore-past-order.rationale: Bonald tied family and social order to tradition and opposed the revolutionary break; modern familialists speak of a collapse of the family.

direct-action.rationale: Not a familialist method; its parties work through elections.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Familialism is built on the settled nuclear family and civilization (the article calls the family the foundation of civilization).

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The article says traditional thinkers assigned set roles within the family; abolishing division of labor is the opposite.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim; Marx and Engels appear in the article as critics of familialism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A Marxist doctrine opposed to familialism's critics and its social order.

collective-farming.rationale: Bonald's agrarian writing centers the agricultural family, not collective farming.

taxation-theft.rationale: Familialism asks the state for family tax allowances (Cameron's marriage allowance in the article) and does not treat taxation as theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Familiaris Consortio and family-values politics support law that upholds moral norms for marriage and sexuality beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Familiaris Consortio speaks of family rights as distinct from individual ones, and the family is the unit of society in familialism.

state-as-business.rationale: Familialism models the state on the family, not on a business with customers.

total-state.rationale: Familiaris Consortio says parents' educational right is inalienable and the state must only assist the family, rejecting state direction of every area.

national-rebirth.rationale: Familialists warn of family collapse and national decadence (Quayle, Back to Basics in the article); not a central doctrine.

universal-morality.rationale: Bonald held that moral principles descend from divinely given tradition and Familiaris Consortio states universal norms on marriage.

single-common-good.rationale: Familiaris Consortio presents the family as the means of humanizing society and ties family rights to the common good.

school-vouchers.rationale: Familiaris Consortio (paras 36, 40) says parents' educational right is original and inalienable, including the right to choose a school that matches the family's faith.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Bonald argued reason cannot reach religion without tradition and revelation, and the article ties familialism to Christian teaching.

class-collaboration.rationale: Bonald's guild restoration and organic social view favored cooperation between social orders over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Familialism values inherited institutions and tradition.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The article says traditional thinkers assigned set roles, but Familiaris Consortio (para 23) also affirms women's access to public functions; split on law in public life.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist claim; the family-state analogy casts the state as a family-like order rather than class instrument.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The article describes familialism as assigning authority to the father; the claim that society is structurally biased against women conflicts with this.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Familiaris Consortio condemns state limits on couples' procreation decisions and public coercion on childbearing.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Familiaris Consortio and familialist parties expect the state to protect and support families, beyond a minimal role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not a familialist doctrine; Catholic family teaching leans against it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Familiaris Consortio affirms the equal dignity of women and men and condemns discrimination against unmarried mothers and widows (paras 22, 24).

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Familiaris Consortio holds parents are entitled to an education conforming to their faith, which favors religious instruction available in schools.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Bonald found the people's share in power absurd while modern familialists accept democratic consent; split.

separated-powers.rationale: Bonald thought separation of powers led toward anarchy; modern familialist movements take no stated position on it.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine alien to familialism and its social order.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Familiaris Consortio stresses solidarity with families in need, but no ranking of the poor is in the sources.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Familiaris Consortio welcomes children and rejects population-control programs framed on that premise.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Bonald favored a strong monarch but modern familialism is silent.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Familiaris Consortio is a Catholic text, but familialism as a whole is not tied to church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Catholic familialism keeps the Church to teaching and assisting, not ruling.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not a familialist doctrine; a Leninist position inconsistent with national and family loyalty.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Home ownership is family-friendly but a ban on renting is not a familialist demand.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Bonald's agrarian family writing favored rural family life; modern sources are silent.

death-penalty.rationale: Catholic familialism and US Christian-right familialism diverge here.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Familiaris Consortio (para 37) says sex education belongs to parents under subsidiarity, with schools only assisting; the US right backs abstinence-only teaching.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Family-values groups such as Focus on the Family and the Family Research Council campaign for restrictions; Familiaris Consortio defends marital sexuality.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Familiaris Consortio defends parents' right to faith-conforming education; family-values groups seek conscience exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Familialism values custom and the traditional family form over alternative ways of living.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Catholic social teaching supports aid, but familialism as such is silent.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Familiaris Consortio asks the state to help the Church and parents in education and rejects state curbing of religion.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Bonald cast the monarch as embodying the general will, but not as divine descent.

character-from-environment.rationale: Familialism holds the family forms the child's character; the Wikipedia article and its critics debate whether the family structure matters more than parenting.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Bonald's monarch rules for society's good under natural law, not above law.

equal-parenting.rationale: The article notes opposition to non-traditional families; equal-time custody splits fathers' rights and mother-primacy adherents.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist claim inapplicable to familialism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Bonald defended primogeniture and landed family estates; redistribution cuts against it.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Marxist claim; Engels's view on family origins is cited as a critique of familialism.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Familialism assigns distinct roles in family and treats parity quotas as non-traditional; Familiaris Consortio endorses women's access to public roles without quotas.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Not a familialist position; Bonald opposed revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Bonald defended primogeniture and hereditary family estates; the article cites familialism supporting monarchy and aristocracy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist claim not held by familialism.

elective-rulers.rationale: Bonald supported hereditary monarchy but modern familialism accepts elections.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Bonald favored a strong monarch; modern familialists accept parliaments.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Familiaris Consortio urges families to take an active role in shaping laws and institutions that protect family rights.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim not held by familialism.

paid-care-work.rationale: Familiaris Consortio (para 23) says work in the home deserves respect and mothers should not be forced to work outside, and familialist welfare (Wikipedia) rests on family care.

filial-duty.rationale: Familialist welfare regimes expect families to care for their members, and the Wikipedia article ties it to mutual obligations within families; filial support is core.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Familiaris Consortio (para 20) reaffirms marriage as indissoluble, and Bonald won repeal of French divorce law in 1815 (source 3).

land-use-tenure.rationale: Bonald defended the landed family estate and inheritance, opposed to communal tenure.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The Wikipedia article places natalism with familialism and cites Cameron's marriage allowance; family-focused parties back state support for births.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Familialism holds that marriage and the family are the basis of society; abolishing marriage as an institution is a view held by its critics (Engels).

religion-illusion.rationale: Bonald held the Church and tradition as sources of moral truth and the article ties familialism to Christian teaching.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Familialism does not treat the economic system as the cause of gender roles; Marxist writers (Engels, Healy) make the claim.

socialized-care.rationale: The article defines familialist welfare as expecting families, not the state, to care for members, contrasted with Nordic defamilialized care.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Bonald attacked both laissez-faire and revolution, but modern familialists are split.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a familialist claim; the sources never present it.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A critical-theory claim not held by familialism.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist claim not held by familialism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Bonald grounded authority in God and the Church, and the family father's authority was cited from scripture in the article.

property-franchise.rationale: Bonald opposed democracy but modern familialism does not call for property qualifications.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim not held by familialism, which assigns authority to the father.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Familiaris Consortio reaffirms indissolubility and rejects contraception, resisting reinterpretation of family doctrine.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Familiaris Consortio defends parents' right to religious education against state ideology.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Familialism values social order; abolition is foreign to it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Familialist welfare relies on families and communities rather than the state for care, which supports charity and local help over state aid.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The article says traditional thinkers made the father the authority, while Familiaris Consortio (paras 22, 23) asserts equal dignity; strands split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Familialism has no stated view; family inheritance and family wages pull in different directions.

family-wage.rationale: Familialism puts the household at the centre, and Familiaris Consortio asks society to organise so families can live on a worker's earnings and mothers are not forced out to work.

person-over-state.rationale: Familiaris Consortio holds that the person is the origin and goal of social life and that the state must serve the person and family.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Familiaris Consortio treats the family as a domestic church and human life as more than material; the strand is rooted in Christian teaching.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Familialism has no stated environmental-tax position, and its adherents split along general conservative and centrist lines.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Familiaris Consortio affirms women's dignity and distinct role in family and society and asks that it be honoured, though it frames this around family and motherhood.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The exhortation grounds the dignity of the person and the family in a created human nature that is not ours to remake.

premarital-sex.rationale: Familialism defends marriage as the proper setting for sex and opposes alternative arrangements, so it rejects the acceptability of sex outside marriage.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Catholic familialism treats scripture as authoritative but not as literalist, and Bonald-style traditionalism does not stress inerrancy; adherents are split.

national-church-status.rationale: Bonald wanted Catholicism restored as the state religion, and Catholic and family-values movements generally favour religion's public recognition.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Familialism opposes divorce, so a wife initiating divorce without her husband's consent runs against its documented stance.

missingStatements.text: The state should give married couples with children tax and benefit advantages over other households.
missingStatements.rationale: The article cites David Cameron's marriage tax allowance and family-focused parties as familialist policy.

missingStatements.text: Parents, not the state, have the primary right and duty to educate their children.
missingStatements.rationale: Familiaris Consortio calls parents' educational right original, primary, irreplaceable and inalienable.

missingStatements.text: Marriage should be lifelong and divorce should be made difficult or prohibited.
missingStatements.rationale: Familiaris Consortio reaffirms indissolubility, and Bonald won repeal of French divorce law in 1815.

missingStatements.text: Society should be organised so that mothers are not effectively forced to work outside the home.
missingStatements.rationale: Familiaris Consortio para 23 asks society to be structured so mothers are not pushed out of the home against their wishes.

notes: Strands differ: Bonald's absolutist monarchism, Catholic social teaching, US Christian-right family values, and Southern European unsupported familialism. Economic positions vary widely across them, hence many neutral low-confidence answers.
